summary.text: A 28-year-old woman was admitted with a right submandibular mass that had re-swelled 5 years after the initial surgical removal. She had undergone resection of a right submandibular mass at another hospital 10 years prior, with pathology considered a mixed tumor; the tumor recurred five years ago and gradually enlarged, and B-ultrasound showed solid nodules. Examination found a firm oval 3.0×2.0 cm mass, a surgical scar and palpable right neck lymph nodes.

MRI on the first day of admission showed multiple round nodules in the right submandibular gland with a central unenhanced necrotic area, a capsule sign and enlarged enhancing right neck lymph nodes, and recurrence was suspected. CT on the second day showed multiple low-density nodules with uneven enhancement, and a puncture biopsy on day 2 gave PA.

She underwent right submandibular gland and mass resection, cervical lymph node resection and skin flap arthroplasty. The specimen showed multiple greyish-white solid nodules, and histology with immunohistochemistry led to a pathological diagnosis of recurrent, multifocal PA with mild to moderate atypical hyperplasia, malignant potential and suspected lymph node involvement. Radiotherapy was not performed.
